steps: Weigh one batch: 26 lb Mulcoa 70 calcined mullite grog (Clay Art Center's "CE70"), 15 lb Greenstripe fireclay, 4 lb Raw kyanite (Virginia Kyanite), 5 lb Dextrin, and 12 lb of water (24.0 % of the dry mix). 18 batches cover the lining with 10 % to spare.
Mix the dry ingredients first, then add the water and mix to an even paste.
Fold in foam until the mix is 55 % of the cast volume air: a level US quart of it then weighs 1.86 lb (845 g). Weigh a quart from each batch and add foam or mix to correct it.
Cast it, and from the same batch cast test pieces to fire and measure.
Nothing in this mix sets with water: it holds only by drying, and stays weak until it is fired. Keep it dry, and support it until then.
Dry it out and fire it on the schedule below.
Fire test pieces to the kiln's top temperature, measure their fired density and shrinkage, and enter them under measured: they replace the estimates here.

findings.message: Heat loss is the steady loss with the kiln held at top temperature. It does not include the heat stored in the walls and ware during the firing.

Cylinders joined in parallel are assumed to add their capacities. That is a reasonable inference at the same temperature and fill, but no source states it. Never warm a cylinder with a flame or heater.
Gas piping, regulators, safety valves and the installation must be done or checked by a licensed gas fitter to your local code (NFPA 54 and 58 in the US).
The right wall is the door: bricked up, dry, for each firing. Lay the inner and outer courses together, staggered, with a header course two-thirds of the way up.
Side-mounted burners need a bag wall so the flames don't hit the ware: hard brick, first course solid in front of the burners.
Damper: a kiln shelf in a slot 16.5 in wide and one course high, about a foot above the top of the flue. Brace the chimney with angle at its corners and tie it to the kiln frame.

Three spy holes, 2¼ × 2½ in (a quarter brick), in the door: about 8 in above the floor, midway and near the top, a few inches off centre so they miss the shelf posts. Cone packs in the top and bottom, draw rings in the middle.

The skewbacks and the fill beside the arch are drawn along the arch's radius at the springline and counted by volume. A 60° skewback is the usual choice. The steel that takes the arch's thrust is in the frame.

Prices were checked on 2026-10-21 and will change. Steel is listed by length, with 10 % extra, but not priced. Hardware, electrical parts (relays, controller, wiring), gas fittings and shipping are not included.
